legend: Continued fractions are a powerful mathematical tool. They are however, too complicated, so we have created our own definition.

Let (a,b)$$$(a, b)$$$ be a pair of positive integers. We call the sequence {a+nb+n}∞n=0$$$\left \{\frac{a+n}{b+n} \right\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$$$ the continued fractions of the pair (a,b)$$$(a, b)$$$. For example, if a=14$$$a = 14$$$ and b=2$$$b = 2$$$, the sequence of continued fractions begins with 142$$$\frac{14}{2}$$$, 153$$$\frac{15}{3}$$$, 164$$$\frac{16}{4}$$$, 175$$$\frac{17}{5}$$$, 186$$$\frac{18}{6}$$$, 197$$$\frac{19}{7}$$$.

Note that if a≠b$$$a \neq b$$$ the sequence of continued fractions contains only a finite number of integers. In the above example, the elements that are integers are those with indices n=0,1,2,4,10$$$n = 0, 1, 2, 4, 10$$$.

We define the integrity of a pair of integers (a,b)$$$(a, b)$$$ to be the length of the longest prefix of the sequence of continued fractions that contains only integers. For example integrity(14,2)=3$$$\textrm{integrity}(14, 2) = 3$$$.
You are given a positive integer p$$$p$$$. Your task is to find and report all pairs of integers (a,b)$$$(a, b)$$$ that satisfy the following two conditions:
input: The first line of input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤20$$$1 \leq t \leq 20$$$) — the number of test cases.

t$$$t$$$ lines follow (one for each test case), the i$$$i$$$-th of which (1≤i≤t$$$1 \leq i \leq t$$$) is containing a single integer pi$$$p_i$$$ (2≤pi≤1018$$$2 \leq p_i \leq 10^{18}$$$) — corresponding to the p$$$p$$$ from the description above.
output: For each test case, first output one line containing a single integer k$$$k$$$  – the number of pairs (a,b)$$$(a, b)$$$ satisfying the two conditions from the problem statement. Then output k$$$k$$$ integers b1,b2,…,bk$$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_k$$$ — the values of b$$$b$$$ sorted in ascending order.
Note that under the constraints of the problem it can be shown that the sum of all k$$$k$$$ is at most 100000$$$100\,000$$$.
